questions.prompt: What is observability?

options.text: The ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs
The ability to deploy software faster
The number of unit tests in a system

questions.explanation: Observability is the ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs (telemetry: traces, metrics, logs).

questions.prompt: Distributed tracing is based on which three main signal types?
questions.explanation: Distributed tracing is based on three signals: logs, spans, and traces.

questions.prompt: What does a span represent?

options.text: A single unit of work or operation, with name, timing, and attributes
The entire request path across all services

questions.explanation: A span represents a single unit of work/operation triggered by a request, containing a name, time-related data, log messages, and attributes.

questions.prompt: What is the first span of a trace called?
questions.explanation: A trace is made of one or more spans; the first one is the root span, representing the request from start to finish.

questions.prompt: Which metric instrument kind accumulates over time but can also go down again (e.g. queue length)?
questions.explanation: An UpDownCounter accumulates but can decrease (e.g. queue length); a Counter only goes up, a Gauge reads a current value, a Histogram aggregates client-side (e.g. latencies).

questions.prompt: Which statements about SLI and SLO are correct?

options.text: An SLI measures the behavior of the system, often capturing the user perspective
An SLO attaches business value to one or more SLIs
An SLI is a contract penalty clause
An SLO is a type of log format

questions.explanation: An SLI (Service Level Indicator) measures system behavior, often from the user perspective; an SLO (Service Level Objective) attaches business value to SLIs.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between sampling and tracing in profiling?

options.text: Sampling periodically interrupts the program with low overhead; tracing instruments calls with high detail but higher overhead
Sampling is more precise but slower than tracing
Tracing has lower overhead than sampling

questions.explanation: Sampling periodically interrupts and records the CPU state (low overhead, statistically accurate); tracing/instrumentation records function calls with high detail but higher overhead.

questions.prompt: In a flamegraph, the width of a function box represents how frequently that function was present in the collected samples.
questions.explanation: Flamegraph: the y-axis is stack depth, the x-axis spans the sample collection (alphabetical, not time), and box width is the frequency of that function in samples.

questions.prompt: OpenTelemetry is best described as:

options.text: An open-source, vendor- and tool-agnostic observability framework for generating, exporting, and collecting telemetry

questions.explanation: OpenTelemetry is an open-source, vendor- and tool-agnostic observability framework for the generation, export, and collection of traces, metrics, and logs.

questions.prompt: Which of these are valid OpenTelemetry span kinds?
questions.explanation: Span kinds are Client, Server, Internal, Producer, and Consumer; Gauge is a metric instrument kind, not a span kind.

questions.prompt: What characterizes a structured log?

options.text: It follows a consistent schema or typed fields (e.g. JSON)
It has no consistent structure and is hard to parse
It is always binary and unreadable

questions.explanation: Structured logs use a consistent schema or typed fields (e.g. JSON); unstructured logs lack consistent structure, and semistructured logs mix key/value pairs without a stable schema.

questions.prompt: Which standard HTTP header field carries trace context between components?
questions.explanation: The standard traceparent HTTP header carries version, trace-id, parent-id, and trace-flags so all spans of one trace can be related.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a Counter and a Gauge?

options.text: A Counter accumulates over time; a Gauge measures a current value at the moment it is read
A Counter can go down; a Gauge cannot
A Gauge aggregates request latencies into buckets

questions.explanation: A Counter accumulates over time, while a Gauge measures a current value at read time; a Histogram aggregates values such as latencies into buckets.

questions.prompt: Why is profiling useful?

options.text: It identifies which program elements to optimize, avoiding wasted effort on low-impact methods
It replaces the need for tests

questions.explanation: Profiling makes programs more efficient and developers more productive by identifying which elements to optimize; without it you risk optimizing low-impact methods.

questions.prompt: Java Flight Recorder (JFR) is a low-overhead profiling and monitoring system built into the JVM that stores events in a compact .jfr file.
questions.explanation: JFR is a low-overhead profiling/monitoring system built into the JVM; it records CPU, memory, GC, threads, and I/O events into a compact .jfr file for later analysis.

questions.prompt: Which are profile types described in the lecture?

options.text: Off-CPU (time blocked, not running on a CPU)

questions.explanation: Profile types include On-CPU, stall cycles, Memory, I/O, and Off-CPU (time a thread is blocked, e.g. waiting on I/O or locks).

questions.prompt: Which fields describe a metric instrument?
questions.explanation: A metric instrument captures a measurement and is described by its Name, Kind, Unit, and Description.

questions.prompt: What does telemetry data (traces, metrics, logs) allow you to do?

options.text: Troubleshoot and handle novel problems (unknown unknowns)
Understand the motivation for system behavior (why is this happening?)

questions.explanation: Telemetry lets you detect problems, troubleshoot novel ones (unknown unknowns), and understand why the system behaves as it does.

questions.prompt: How do JFR's two predefined settings differ?

options.text: 'default' has very low overhead and no execution sampling; 'profile' adds execution sampling and allocation profiling at higher overhead
'default' adds allocation profiling; 'profile' disables all events

questions.explanation: JFR 'default' focuses on GC/locks/I/O/JVM internals with very low overhead (no jdk.ExecutionSample); 'profile' enables execution sampling and allocation profiling (~1–2% overhead), suitable for flamegraphs.

questions.prompt: How is a distributed trace visualized over time?

options.text: As a waterfall diagram of its spans
As a flamegraph of stack samples

questions.explanation: A distributed trace's spans are commonly shown as a waterfall diagram; flamegraphs instead represent stack samples for profiling.

questions.prompt: Which log format is shown in this slide example?
questions.explanation: A consistent JSON schema with typed fields is a structured log. Source: SwD&A Observability slides (Marco Torchiano) — 'Structured Log (JSON)' example.

questions.prompt: In this Common Log Format line from the slides, what do the final two fields, 200 and 9481, mean?

options.text: The HTTP response status code and the response size in bytes
The client IP and the user id
The request timestamp and HTTP method

questions.explanation: In CLF, 200 is the HTTP response status code and 9481 is the response size in bytes (alice is the userid, 192.168.1.30 the client IP). Source: SwD&A Observability slides — 'Common Log Format (CLF)'.

questions.prompt: The W3C traceparent header shown in the slides is below. What are its four fields, in order?
questions.explanation: The standard traceparent header carries version, trace-id, parent-id, and trace-flags so spans of one trace can be related. Source: SwD&A Observability slides — 'Context propagation'.

questions.prompt: What does this command from the slides do?

options.text: Runs the app with a Java Flight Recorder profiling session, recording 30s into a .jfr file
Compiles the program into a .jfr archive
Runs the unit tests for 30 seconds
Starts a web server on the profiling port

questions.explanation: It launches the app with JFR started from the begin, recording for 30 seconds into profiling-recording.jfr. Source: SwD&A Observability slides — 'JFR Profiling Session'.
